'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**Three people are killed and 15 others injured by a bombing during prayers at a [[mosque]] in [[Spin Ghar]], [[Nangarhar Province]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/12/blast-at-mosque-in-afghanistans-nangarhar-province (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[Cessna 172]] crashes in [[Hampton Township, New Jersey]], [[United States]], killing two people, including businessman and [[space tourist]] [[Glen de Vries]]. [https://eu.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2021/11/12/new-jersey-plane-crash-victims-include-man-who-went-space/8589950002/ (USA Today)]
*Two [[Russian Armed Forces|Russia]]n [[paratrooper]]s are killed during [[Military exercise|military drills]] near the [[Belarus–Poland border|Polish border]] in western [[Belarus]]. The [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Ministry of Defence]] says their [[parachute]]s failed to deploy properly "due to a sudden strong gust of wind" during their jumps. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/11/12/two-russian-paratroopers-die-in-belarus-during-joint-exercises-near-polish-border (Euronews)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] delays the reopening of nightlife entertainment venues to January 15 due to concerns about ventilation and inefficient prevention measures in pubs, bars and [[karaoke]] venues. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/bangkok-thailand-covid-tourism-b1956399.html?amp (''The Independent'')]
****Thailand surpasses two million cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/asia/thailands-covid-19-cases-surpass-2-million20211112115426 (Asian News International)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Government of Japan|government]] announces that they will obtain 1.6 million doses of [[Merck & Co.]]'s [[molnupiravir]] and have also increased hospital capacities for COVID-19 patients to 30% in order to prepare for a sixth wave of the pandemic. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/11/ba7b19eb1b59-japan-opts-to-secure-covid-oral-medicine-for-16-mil-people.html (Kyodo News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Denmark]] reintroduces its [[Vaccine passports during the COVID-19 pandemic|digital pass]] that must be used in nightclubs, cafés, indoor seating at restaurants, and at outdoor events with more than 2,000 people as it reclassifies COVID-19 as "a socially critical disease" amid an increase in new cases. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-europe-denmark-health-4cc1b9811d21003905d7a6a2fee41837 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****[[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|caretaker prime minister]] [[Mark Rutte]] announces a three-week partial [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] that requires bars, restaurants, and shops to close at certain times and reintroduces {{cvt|1.5|m}} [[social distancing]] measures beginning tomorrow. The Netherlands is the first country in [[Western Europe]] to impose a lockdown since the summer. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/nov/12/partial-lockdown-in-netherlands-amid-record-covid-cases (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mauritius]]
***[[Mauritius]] imposes new restrictions that limit the number of people in large gatherings such as funerals, weddings, and rallies amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases despite high [[COVID-19 vaccination in Mauritius|vaccination]] rates. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211112-mauritius-imposes-new-virus-curbs-as-cases-jump (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Eritrea–United States relations]]
**The [[U.S. Treasury Department]] imposes sanctions on the [[Eritrean Military]] and other [[Eritrea]]-based entities and individuals in an attempt to bring an end to the [[Tigray War]]. The sanctions also blacklist the [[Politics of Eritrea|Eritrean ruling party]] [[People's Front for Democracy and Justice]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/us-blacklists-eritrean-military-over-conflict-ethiopia-2021-11-12/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis]], [[Belarus–Iraq relations]]
**[[Iraq]] restricts direct flights to [[Belarus]] amid the [[migrant crisis]] in at the [[Belarus–Poland border]]. [https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/26229-Iraq-halts-direct-flights-with-Belarus-amid-migrant-crisis (Kurdistan 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack]]
**[[United States Attorney General|U.S. Attorney General]] [[Merrick Garland]] announces that former [[Counselor to the President|White House Chief Strategist]] [[Steve Bannon]] has been charged by the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Department of Justice]] for refusing to testify before the [[January 6th Committee|January 6 select committee]] investigating the [[United States Capitol|U.S. Capitol]] [[2021 United States Capitol attack|riot]] and also refusing to provide documents requested by the committee. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/former-trump-adviser-steve-bannon-indicted-federal-grand-jury-contempt-n1283834 (NBC News)]
*[[Britney Spears conservatorship dispute]]
**American singer [[Britney Spears]] is released from her 13-year [[conservatorship]] in accordance with a ruling by judge [[Brenda J. Penny]] of the [[Los Angeles County Superior Court]], following allegations of abuse originating from fan speculation, media investigation, and public testimony. [https://mb.com.ph/2021/11/13/judge-dissolves-britney-spears-guardianship/ (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]
*[[Americans|American]] journalist [[Danny Fenster]] is [[sentence (law)|sentenced]] by a [[Tatmadaw|Myanmar military]] court to 11 years in prison, after being found guilty of three [[criminal charge|charges]] brought against him. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/11/12/media/danny-fenster-myanmar-sentence-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[European Commission]] announces its intention to bring the [[government of Portugal]] to the [[European Court of Justice]] over persistent violations of [[Directive 2008/50/EC]], which limits the amount of certain emissions a country can produce in order to regulate [[air pollution]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/eu-sues-portugal-poor-air-quality-caused-by-nitrogen-dioxide-2021-11-12/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Latvia]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**The [[Saeima]] votes 62–7 with two abstentions and 29 absent lawmakers to ban [[Member of Parliament|MP]]s who refuse to be [[COVID-19 vaccination in Latvia|vaccinated]] against COVID-19 from voting and participating in the [[parliament of Latvia|parliament]], both for in-person and remote meetings. The restrictions will be in effect from November 15 until July 1. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/latvia-bans-unvaccinated-lawmakers-meetings-81129693 (ABC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/latvia-bans-unvaccinated-lawmakers-voting-docks-pay-2021-11-12 (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of El Salvador]]
**The [[Legislative Assembly of El Salvador|Legislative Assembly]] begins to discuss [[President of El Salvador|president]] [[Nayib Bukele]]'s proposal to [[Media censorship|regulate criticism]] of the [[government of El Salvador|government]] by civil organizations and media critics of the government. [https://elpais.com/internacional/2021-11-11/bukele-emula-una-de-las-leyes-represivas-de-ortega-para-acallar-la-critica-en-el-salvador.html (''El País'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 Winter Olympics]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[government of China|China]] reports the first cases of COVID-19 among foreign athletes who will participate in the [[Winter Olympics]], with two [[luge|lugers]] from an unidentified nation testing positive. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/two-foreign-athletes-test-positive-covid-19-run-up-beijing-winter-olympics-2021-11-12/ (Reuters)]
